fixes.explanation: Close in distance, but not the right place. The Mount of Olives is a hill outside the city (Acts 1:12), and John doesn't set this scene there. Jesus found the sellers and the money changers in the temple courts (John 2:14). It's one of those answers that sounds right until you check the verse.
A whip is right. John says Jesus "…made a whip out of cords…" (John 2:15). Cords in, whip out. I couldn't build anything useful from a pile of cords, so I admire the skill.

True. John says Jesus "…drove all from the temple courts, both sheep and cattle." (John 2:15). The sheep and cattle are named right there in the verse. I bet that was a LOUD moment, with hooves going everywhere.

It's actually true, friend. The text says Jesus "…drove all from the temple courts, both sheep and cattle." (John 2:15). The sheep and cattle are named among those driven out. It's easy to think only the sellers went and the animals stayed, but the verse says otherwise.
That's it. John says Jesus "…poured out the coins of the money changers and overturned their tables." (John 2:15). Coins everywhere, tables flipped. I bet those coins made quite a racket.

Marketplace, baker, you nailed it! Jesus says, "How dare you turn My Father’s house into a marketplace!" (John 2:16). Listen to how He puts it: "My Father’s house." That's the name He gives the place.
Not quite, friend. Jesus says, "How dare you turn My Father’s house into a marketplace!" (John 2:16). He doesn't say anything about a prison. What He names is a marketplace in His Father's house.
Rest is a good Bible theme, but it's not what they remember here. John says the disciples recalled, "Zeal for Your house will consume Me." (John 2:17). That's about zeal for God's house.
Forty-six it is. The Jews say, "This temple took forty-six years to build…" (John 2:20). That's a long time to build something. I think hearing someone talk about three days sounded wild to them.

Seven is a number people love in the Bible, so I get it. But the Jews say, "This temple took forty-six years to build…" (John 2:20). Seven years would be quick by comparison. Then they ask Jesus if He is going to raise it up in three days.

Twenty is a nice round number, but it's not the one in the verse. The Jews say, "This temple took forty-six years to build…" (John 2:20). That's more than double your guess. Forty-six years! My cookies are done in twelve minutes, so that number makes my head spin.

Solomon, David's son and Israel's king (1 Kings 2:12; 4:1), did build a temple (1 Kings 6:1). But that's not what Jesus meant. John says, "…Jesus was speaking about the temple of His body." (John 2:21). The Jews took it the building way, and that's where the confusion came from.

Right on time. John says, "After He was raised from the dead, His disciples remembered that He had said this." (John 2:22). That's when the memory comes up, after the resurrection. Then, "…they believed the Scripture and the word that Jesus had spoken." (John 2:22).

That's the reason John gives. "…Jesus did not entrust Himself to them, for He knew them all." (John 2:24). Verse 25 adds that He "…did not need any testimony about man…" (John 2:25). The reason is right there in the text.
